Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
635 AM EDT Wed Sep 2 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 306 AM EDT Wednesday...

No significant changes were made with this forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 306 AM EDT Wednesday...

1. Gusty south winds will increase today. Widespread rainfall 
will move in this evening into tonight, with periods of moderate to 
locally heavy rain expected along with some embedded thunderstorms. 

2. Some scattered afternoon showers are possible each day 
Thursday through Saturday, then we become drier Sunday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 306 AM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: This afternoon into tonight will be one of the more 
active periods this week as a low pressure system to our north drags 
a series of fronts through our forecast area. The day will start off 
dry, but rain will move in from the west during the afternoon hours 
as a warm front approaches. Increasing southerly flow ahead of the 
system will result in developing gusty southerly winds today, 
especially over Lake Champlain where gusts will reach 20 to 30+
knots by this afternoon into this evening and a Lake Wind
Advisory is in effect. Outside of Lake Champlain, highest gusts
this afternoon will mainly be observed over the northern 
Champlain Valley, higher elevations of the Greens and 
Adirondacks, and over the northern slopes of the Adirondacks. 
Gusts will be strongest ahead of the steady rain, then will 
diminish as rain becomes widespread due to low- level 
stabilization. 

The increased southerly flow will bring PWats to 1.5 to 2.0 inches 
by this evening, which is around 150 to 200% of climatological 
normal for our area for this time of year. This anomalously 
moist air mass will support some periods of moderate to heavy 
rain this evening into tonight. Models are indicating rates will
mainly remain under a tenth of an inch an hour, but some 
heavier showers and thunderstorms could produce brief rainfall 
rates up to a quarter to a half inch an hour. Overall, the flood
risk this evening into tonight is low (WPC's Excessive Rainfall
Outlook has our entire area in a marginal risk of rainfall 
exceeding flash flood guidance). However, if any heavier storms 
track over the same area, those areas will need to be watched 
closely. 

In addition to moderate to briefly heavy rainfall, some (mainly 
elevated) thunderstorms are anticipated this evening into early 
tonight. The surface based instability and overall severe threat 
will be limited by a maintained low level inversion over most areas. 
However, the environment is slightly more favorable locally over the 
southern Saint Lawrence Valley, where the development of some 
marginal SBCAPE is progged.  The amount of surface based instability 
is still somewhat in question, but latest SPC Convective Outlook 
maintains the Marginal Risk for most of Saint Lawrence County, with 
the Slight Risk staying just to our southwest. The main threat from 
thunderstorms in northern New York will be gusty winds and locally 
heavy rainfall. The remainder of our forecast area remains within 
the General Thunder contour, and risk of severe weather outside of 
the Saint Lawrence Valley is low tonight.

KEY MESSAGE 2:  Widespread rainfall will come to an end by Thursday 
morning, giving way to generally drier weather with afternoon 
showers possible each day through Saturday.  A slow moving upper-
level low will linger to our north/northeast through Saturday, 
supporting seasonably cool conditions with periods of instability-
driven afternoon showers.  Coverage of showers will be greatest over 
higher terrain. Meanwhile, the Champlain Valley and Saint Lawrence 
Valley will remain mainly dry during this timeframe. By Sunday,
any remaining shower activity will end as ridging builds in 
from the west. Subsidence will allow for more sunshine and a 
pleasant, albeit seasonably cool, day.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 12Z Thursday...Ceilings will generally lift through the
morning, with most TAF sites expected to be VFR between 13Z and
00Z. After 00Z, ceilings will again begin to lower towards MVFR
levels as widespread rain spreads into the area. Rain showers 
will be moderate to heavy at times, which will result in 
intervals of IFR visibility...mainly between 22Z and 06Z 
tonight. Some embedded thunderstorms are possible later this 
evening into tonight, especially over the Saint Lawrence Valley.
These storms may produce briefly gusty winds 40+ knots from 
variable directions, along with cloud to ground lightning. 
Ceilings will further lower to low MVFR/IFR levels
after 06Z as moisture is trapped below a strengthening low 
level inversion. 

Winds will mostly be southerly/southeasterly early 
this morning and under 10 KT. Winds will increase significantly 
after 14Z, with southerly gusts in the 15-25 KT range for most 
areas, with gusts up to 30 KT possible in the Champlain Valley. 
Some areas of LLWS are expected this evening into tonight. 

Outlook...

Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
South winds 10 to 20 knots this morning will increase to 20 to 
30 knots by this afternoon into this evening. Waves will start 
off 1 to 3 feet this afternoon, then build to 2 to 4+ feet by 
late tonight. Winds will be strongest this evening into the 
early overnight hours, then will decrease once steady rain 
develops. Winds on Thursday will be 15 to 20 knots in the 
morning, then become light and variable later in the day.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Duell
AVIATION...Duell
MARINE...Duell
